title: Prawn Fried Rice
subtitle: Quick wok-fried rice with king prawns
excerpt: Day-old rice is the secret here. Freshly cooked rice steams rather than fries, so plan ahead. The whole dish takes about 15 minutes once everything is prepped and on the hob.
sourceNotes: Fried rice is a staple across Chinese home cooking and was a practical way to use leftover cooked rice. The Cantonese version with egg and spring onion is the template for countless adaptations worldwide.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the rice the day before and refrigerate uncovered. Cold, dry rice fries far better than freshly cooked.

content.text: Get the wok as hot as possible before adding any oil. A properly hot wok gives colour and flavour rather than a steamed, soggy result.

items.prepNote: cooked the day before and refrigerated

content.text: Heat the wok over a very high heat until it just starts to smoke.
Add 2 tablespoons of the oil. Add the prawns in a single layer.
Cook for 90 seconds each side until pink and just cooked. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Add the garlic, ginger, and white parts of the spring onion.
Add the cold rice. Break up any clumps. Fry for 3 minutes, pressing the rice against the wok.
Push the rice to the sides. Pour the beaten eggs into the centre.
Scramble the eggs briefly, then fold through the rice before they fully set.
Add the peas. Stir for 1 minute until heated through.
Return the prawns. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss everything together.
Scatter over the green spring onion tops. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Rice clumps and steams rather than frying.
items.cause: Rice was too fresh or wok not hot enough.
items.fix: Use cold day-old rice. Get the wok very hot before adding it.

items.cause: Overcooked. Prawns need only 3 minutes total.
items.fix: Remove as soon as they turn pink. They finish off the heat.

items.cause: Too much soy sauce for the amount of rice.
items.fix: Add soy sauce a little at a time. Taste as you go.
